convergence.description: Gate config-done on the whole cross-vendor fabric converging. PUTs onto examples/mixed-nos.yml. This is also the suite that carries the WORKED EXAMPLES of test-suites v2 (contract delta 17), which the Cisco IOL withdrawal of 2026-08-05 had left without a live second flavor: `ospf_adjacency` dispatches ONE test across FOUR device keys, `ospf_peers_json` shows parse=json + compare with peer router IDs rendered from the lab's facts, and `ospf_peers_textfsm` shows parse=textfsm + compare over parsed records. Nothing is hardcoded — every address and router ID comes from the fact namespace.

ospf_adjacency.description: Each of the four routing platforms holds THREE Full adjacencies — i.e. the full cross-vendor mesh is up, asserted in each platform's own idiom. Deliberately node-agnostic (three Full states, not named peers) so one test serves all four device keys; the named-peer assertions live in the two tests below.

ospf_peers_json.description: parse=json + compare, on the two FRR-based platforms. Asserts the two peers vyos1 and frr1 have in COMMON — chr1 and bird1 — are converged Full, with both router IDs rendered from facts. (Their third neighbour is each other, which is why only these two are named: it keeps one case correct for both nodes.)

ospf_peers_textfsm.description: parse=textfsm + compare on MikroTik CHR: asserts all three of its peers are Full, by router ID from facts. RouterOS has no JSON output, so this is the platform that genuinely needs TextFSM — and it needs the `terse` spelling plus a Twinlab-packaged template, because both ntc-templates mikrotik_routeros OSPF templates were written for RouterOS 6 and cannot parse 7 (see the template's own header). The parsed value is a LIST, hence the root-level `list` compare.

fabric_forwarding.description: The control plane agreeing is not the data plane working: ping CHR's loopback from VyOS, which is only reachable if OSPF programmed the FIB on both. bird1 is deliberately NOT a target here — netlab gives a daemon-role node a router ID but no loopback INTERFACE, so its ID is not an address (see the definition's header).

interactive_transport.description: Proves the runner's persistent netmiko channel works on MikroTik CHR — the `interactive: true` path, which needs a netmiko device_type for the platform's ansible_network_os or it returns `no interactive CLI driver for network_os 'routeros'`. CHR was admitted (2026-08-04) without one; the entry `routeros: mikrotik_routeros` was added 2026-08-05 and this is what verifies it against a live box. Runtime stage, so it never gates a configure.

chr_interactive_ping.description: Ping VyOS's loopback from CHR over the netmiko channel rather than a one-shot exec.
